column14: Notes

First king after the Judges, anointed by Samuel at the people's demand. Rejected by God for disobedience at Gilgal, sparing Agag against command, and consulting the medium of Endor. Hebrew text of 1 Sam 13:1 has a numeral gap, so his exact age at accession is unknown; 40-year reign per Acts 13:21.

Installed as rival king over the northern/eastern tribes by Saul's general Abner while David reigned over Judah alone in Hebron. Also called Eshbaal in Chronicles. A weak figurehead controlled by Abner, then abandoned by him; assassinated by his own captains. Not evaluated by the standard did right/evil formula.

Anointed by Samuel years before becoming king; not related to Saul by blood but married his daughter Michal. Reigned 7.5 years in Hebron over Judah alone, then 33 years in Jerusalem over all Israel. Committed adultery with Bathsheba and had Uriah killed, but repented (Psalm 51); reign assessed as right before God overall.

Made king in David's old age, chosen over his elder half-brother Adonijah. Began right - asked God for wisdom, built the Temple - but turned to idolatry in old age due to his foreign wives. Age at accession/death not stated in the text.

Former labor overseer under Solomon; led the ten northern tribes to secede after Rehoboam's harsh response at Shechem. Made golden calves at Bethel and Dan so people would not return to Jerusalem to worship. Kingdom split from Rehoboam in the same year, so no formal synchronism verse is given for his own accession.
Walked in his father's sin.
Assassinated Nadab and exterminated the House of Jeroboam. Condemned by the prophet Jehu son of Hanani for continuing Jeroboam's sins.
Killed while drunk by his chariot commander Zimri; walked in Baasha's sin.
Reigned 7 days. Assassinated Elah and exterminated Baasha's house, then burned the palace over himself when besieged by Omri.
'Did worse than all who were before him.' Proclaimed king by the army after Zimri's death; defeated rival claimant Tibni in a 4-year civil war before ruling alone. Founded Samaria as capital.
Married Jezebel and promoted Baal worship; opposed by Elijah. 'Did more to provoke the LORD than all the kings of Israel before him.'
Served Baal like his parents; consulted Baal-zebub of Ekron when injured.

Brother of Ahaziah, who died without a son. Evil, but 'not like his father and mother' - he removed his father's pillar of Baal. Also dated to the 2nd year of Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 1:17), a second synchronism.

Army commander, not of Omri's bloodline; anointed by a prophet sent by Elisha. Killed Joram of Israel, Ahaziah of Judah, and Jezebel, and destroyed Baal worship - promised a dynasty to the 4th generation - but did not turn from Jeroboam's golden calves. Took the throne mid-year by coup, so no standard accession synchronism is given.
Continued Jeroboam's sins; Israel oppressed by Aram as judgment.
Continued Jeroboam's sins, yet wept for and honored the dying prophet Elisha.
Continued Jeroboam I's sins, though he restored Israel's borders per the word of the prophet Jonah.
Reigned 6 months. His accession fulfilled the promise of a 4-generation dynasty made to Jehu.
Reigned 1 month. Assassinated Zechariah, ending the House of Jehu.
Killed Shallum. Brutally sacked Tiphsah; paid tribute to Assyria's Tiglath-Pileser III (Pul).
Continued Jeroboam's sins.
Assassinated Pekahiah. Allied with Aram against Judah. The 20 years is chronologically difficult against parallel Judah dates; many scholars read it as including a rival/overlapping reign.

Assassinated Pekah with Assyrian backing. Last king of Israel; Samaria fell and the northern tribes were exiled in his 9th year. 'Not like the kings of Israel before him' - comparatively less wicked. Also dated to the 20th year of Jotham (2 Kings 15:30), though Jotham reigned only 16 years - usually explained via a co-regency with Ahaz.

His harsh response to Israel's request for relief caused the ten northern tribes to secede under Jeroboam. 'Did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the LORD'; repented when rebuked by the prophet Shemaiah.
Called Abijam in Kings, Abijah in Chronicles. 'Walked in all the sins his father did,' though Chronicles records a notable victory speech invoking the LORD.
Removed idols and deposed his grandmother Maacah as queen mother. Near the end of his reign he relied on Aram instead of God and imprisoned the seer Hanani for rebuking him.
Sent teachers of the Law throughout Judah. Flawed alliances by marriage and military cooperation with the house of Ahab.
column15: Jehu son of Hanani, Jahaziel, Eliezer, Micaiah

column14: Murdered his brothers; married Athaliah, daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, linking Judah's throne to the Omride dynasty. Died of a severe bowel disease.

Walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, his mother's family; killed by Jehu. Also dated to the 11th year of Joram (2 Kings 9:29), a second synchronism. 2 Chronicles 22:2 (Masoretic Hebrew) gives his age as 42, chronologically impossible (older than his own father, who died at 40); regarded as a scribal error, 22 is used here.

Daughter of Ahab and Jezebel of Israel; the one queen to reign in her own name over Judah or Israel. Seized the throne after her son Ahaziah's death by murdering the rest of the royal family; promoted Baal worship.

Grandson of Athaliah (son of Ahaziah); hidden in the Temple for 6 years during Athaliah's purge, then enthroned by the priest Jehoiada. Did right during Jehoiada's lifetime; after Jehoiada's death he fell into idolatry and had Jehoiada's son Zechariah stoned in the Temple court.
Did right 'yet not with a whole heart' - defeated Edom, then adopted Edomite gods. Killed in a conspiracy after fleeing to Lachish.

Called Azariah in 2 Kings, Uzziah in 2 Chronicles and Isaiah. Sought God under the prophet Zechariah's instruction and prospered greatly, but pride led him to burn incense in the Temple, a priestly duty; God struck him with leprosy for life. Son Jotham likely served as co-regent afterward.
Governed as regent during his father Uzziah's leprosy before formally succeeding him. 'Did what was right... yet the high places were not removed.'
Made his son 'pass through the fire,' worshiped Baal and Aramean gods, and closed/desecrated the Temple.
'Trusted in the LORD; there was none like him among all the kings of Judah.' Removed high places, broke the bronze serpent, restored Temple worship. Granted 15 extra years of life after his illness.

Longest reign of any king. Rebuilt high places, worshiped astral deities, practiced sorcery, sacrificed his own son, and shed much innocent blood - the most wicked king of Judah. 2 Chronicles uniquely records his later captivity in Babylon, repentance, and restoration. No northern king remained to synchronize with, since Israel fell in 722 BC.
Unlike his father Manasseh, he 'did not humble himself.' Assassinated by his own servants.
The Book of the Law was rediscovered in his 18th year, sparking Judah's greatest reform and Passover celebration. Killed at Megiddo fighting Pharaoh Necho II.
Reigned 3 months. Also called Shallum (1 Chron 3:15; Jer 22:11-12). Made king by the people of the land, but deposed by Pharaoh Necho, who installed his brother Jehoiakim instead; died in Egypt.
Installed as a vassal king by Pharaoh Necho, who renamed him from Eliakim to Jehoiakim. Burned the prophet Jeremiah's scroll. Later became a vassal of Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and rebelled.

Reigned 3 months, 10 days. Surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and was deported to Babylon with the Temple treasures and leading citizens; later released and given a pension in the 37th year of exile. 2 Chronicles 36:9 (Masoretic Hebrew) gives his age as 8 vs. 18 in 2 Kings 24:8; 18 is used here as the majority reading.

Uncle of Jehoiachin (son of Josiah, brother of Jehoiakim); placed on the throne as a vassal by Nebuchadnezzar, who renamed him from Mattaniah to Zedekiah. Rebelled against Babylon, leading to Jerusalem's destruction. Witnessed his sons' execution before being blinded and taken to Babylon, where he died. Last king of Judah.
